channel.title: Maricopa County, AZ - News Flash
channel.description: Maricopa County, AZ - Get the latest news

item.title: Get Ready for a Day of Fall Fun at the 2026 Spooktacular Fall Festival!
item.description: Maricopa County WIC and Arizona State University invite families to enjoy a FREE community celebration filled with games, trick-or-treating, music, giveaways, and family fun.

item.title: Maricopa County Celebrates Grand Opening of Family Shelter Housing in Avondale
item.description: Maricopa County recently celebrated the grand opening of Family Bridge Homes, a new temporary housing community in Avondale.

item.title: Supervisor Galvin Honors the Life and Legacy of Senator Jon Kyl
item.description: I am deeply saddened by the passing of former U.S. Senator Jon Kyl, not only for the loss of this great man, but for what his passing represents to all Arizonans. Senator Kyl was a statesman in every sense of the word.

item.title: MCACC Joins BISSELL Pet Foundation’s Empty the Shelters® Adoption Event
item.description: BISSELL Pet Foundation, a national animal welfare organization dedicated to ending pet homelessness, will host its fall Empty the Shelters® adoption event September 21–30, 2026.

item.title: Public Health Reminds Residents to Protect Themselves Against Measles and Seasonal Illnesses
item.description: Risk of measles continues as seasonal respiratory viruses start spreading

item.title: More Speakers Announced: Teen Mental Health Summit
item.description: On Friday, September 25, we’re bringing together students, parents, educators, community leaders, mental health professionals, nonprofits, and more for our second annual East Valley Teen Mental Health Awareness and Violence Prevention Summit.

item.title: Honoring the Lives Lost on September 11, 2001
item.description: On this day, 25 years ago, nearly 3,000 Americans were tragically murdered in the most devastating terrorist attack in U.S. history.

item.title: September Newsletter
item.description: Today, we pause to remember the nearly 3,000 lives lost on September 11, 2001, and honor the courage of the first responders, service members, and everyday Americans who answered the call in the days that followed.

item.title: District 5 September Newsletter
item.description: Thank you to everyone who joined us for our District 5 Summer Program! Throughout the summer, families and students came together to stay active, build new friendships, and enjoy a variety of free recreational opportunities.

item.title: Supervisor Steve Gallardo Offers Condolences to Loved Ones of George Dean
item.description: I am deeply saddened by the passing of my dear friend George Dean, longtime President and CEO of the Greater Phoenix Urban League and a dedicated champion for civil rights, equality and opportunity.

item.title: Maricopa County Awarded $1.5 Million Grant to Expand Services for Incarcerated Veterans
item.description: Maricopa County has been awarded a three-year, $1.5 million grant by the U.S. Department of Labor’s Incarcerated Veterans Transition Program to expand workforce development services...

item.title: Maricopa County Celebrates Grand Opening of Center Bringing Vital Resources to Surprise Residents
Wins Across the Board for Maricopa County!
item.description: Summer isn't slowing Maricopa County down! After a successful Primary, my team and I have spent August out in our district and celebrating our hard-working County staff. I'm eager for temperatures to cool down and a busy fall to start ramping up!

item.title: Maricopa County Regional Parks Bring Back Popular Camping Promotion for County Residents
item.description: Beginning September 18, the Maricopa County Parks and Recreation Department will bring back its popular Buy One, Get One (BOGO) camping promotion, offering County residents an opportunity to enjoy free camping nights at four participating regional parks.

item.title: Eviction Prevention Pilot Launch, Waste Transfer Stations, and Community Updates
item.description: Despite the summer heat, your D3 Team and Maricopa County officials have been very busy. From elections to eviction prevention, from disease-carrying mosquitos to determining the future of our County waste transfer stations, here’s a brief summary.
